items.title: Duffy Jackson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 17, 1995

ctx.x: I stopped Vic Damone’s rehearsal, and took his drummer’s sticks and brushes and cymbals and ten minutes later I was swinging the Basie band. I will never forget that. And the next night we were playing in a place called the Robin Hood Dell, it’s a big amphitheater in Philadelphia. And we bussed it from New York and went to Philly and everything. Now I unfortunately had to wait, they couldn’t stop in New York to get my cymbals, but they put my cymbals on a bus, on a Greyhound, to Philadelphia, and Count Basie…

came back in January of 1985. Count had passed on and Thad Jones took over the band. And that was a very unique experience because the Count Basie Orchestra had never had another leader before. And there was a certain contingent in the orchestra that felt that they didn’t really need a leader. But in one way, to salvage all the work that was being canceled in many ways, the people didn’t want the Count Basie band without the Count. Although we still played the great music and unfortunately the band had to play…
